title: Coherent lifting data compute an operation restriction fiber
statement:
Use spaces, homotopy fibers and coherent diagram spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Let $Q\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be small with $Q_{[0]}$ and $Q_{[1]}$ spaces. Fix $k\geq1$, $C\in Q_{[k]}$, and its inert incidence diagram with edge projections $C_i$ and vertex projections $V_j$. Define $E_C$ to be the space of active arrows to $C$, allowing as source changes only equivalences over identity base arrows, with coherent triangles and all higher simplices; define $E_{C_i}$ in the same way. Let $R:E_C\to\prod_i E_{C_i}$ be restriction by inert block factorization. Fix active arrows $b_i:D_i\to C_i$, with $D_i\in Q_{[n_i]}$, and put $n=\sum_i n_i$. Let $\alpha:[n]\to[k]$ be the active arrow with $\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}(j)=\sum_{i\leq j}n_i$.

Define $L(b)$ to be the coherent space of the following data, allowing every object and every witness to vary. First choose endpoint factorizations of $D_i\xrightarrow{b_i}C_i\to V_{i-1},V_i$ through the inert first and last vertex projections of $D_i$; write the resulting arrows in $Q_{[0]}$ as $u_i^-,u_i^+$. Next choose junction equivalences $e_i:t(D_i)\to s(D_{i+1})$ and homotopies $u_{i+1}^-e_i\simeq u_i^+$. Next choose a source $D\in Q_{[n]}$ and inert block projections, equivalences of these blocks to the specified $D_i$, and their coherent identification with those junction data. The source projections, the $u_i^{\pm}$ and the junction homotopies define maps $D\to V_j$ and endpoint compatibility homotopies with the composites $D\to D_i\xrightarrow{b_i}C_i$. Finally choose a point in the homotopy fiber of the comparison of [lem-coef-operadic-block-incidence-lifting] over this compatible block-and-vertex datum. This last point consists of a map $a:D\to C$ over $\alpha$ and its coherent identification with that incidence datum. The definition of $L(b)$ retains transformations between all these data and every higher simplex, rather than only isomorphism classes or components.

Composing the final incidence identifications with the block equivalences gives a natural equivalence
$$L(b)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{b}(R).$$
It is compatible with restriction in arbitrary simplicial parameter spaces. The assertion includes $n_i=0$ and non-discrete $Q_{[0]}$, and makes no contractibility assertion about $L(b)$.
